Hello all,

I want to train a neural net to do a quad tree depth search faster in x.265 source code. First step is to write a proposal.

If you want to participate, please comment here on how you want to help out.

Thanks, downvotesattractor
Research Project Proposal: Use neural networks to speed up deciding quad-tree depth structure and intra-mode decision logic in x.265 video codec

I am not sure at this point whether I'd be able to help as I have zero experience with neural networks, but I will follow it closely if there is enough interest for it to take off and should I see that there are ways for me to contribute I'd gladly do so.

Best part of research is learning something new right?

Anyway, I'll need a whole bunch of skills for this.

One of the harder problems is training the neural net can take forever. It may be worth investigating how to build a distributed neural net training system that can use unused cpu cycles from people who subscribe to a service to donate their cpu cycles.

Another interesting subproject will be hacking x.265 to generate training data. Generating training data can take forever. I could use help with that too.

A third place where I can use help is to use a OpenGL to implement a superfast neural net.

A fourth place where I can use help is in conducting meetings on IRC with all interested contributors to get the collaboration running smoothly.

Ofcourse, the most interesting part is to see if this project is worth doing at all. What do we gain? What do we loose? Why do it? Can this lead to any useful results worth publishing?

Glad to hear from ya! We are trying to bring in new and current stuff all the time and we love to see new people in here. I look forward to hearing how it was back in the day. :P

Let's see....back in the day, you could smoke indoors, PT was once a year, same 14:30 run time for everyone, and you had the option to walk. No waist measurement, you were over max weight, or you weren't. If you were over, could pass the run and didn't look like shit in uniform, CC could waive it.

Didn't pass urinalysis? Control roster/ UIF (Airman), Lose a stripe (NCO) Discharge (SrNCO). Alcohol use wasn't stigmatized, commanders calls were frequently held in the club with the boss buying the first round afterwards. Workcenters didn't have computers, so no email or internet. Training was live or on video, no powerpoint. I went overseas in '85, came back in '88 and all that had changed or was in the process of changing.

"Work centers didn't have computers" Huh, lets not go to '85 tis a silly place.

I like the weight thing though, it'd be nice for our Cpt. America airmen to not lose points on the Fitness Assessment.

No shit! I've got a guy in my unit, transferred from the Army. He's a borderline body builder. Simply because of his waist though, he fails every time. It's fucking stupid. He can probably carry 2 or 3 people if needed, instead you're failing him for an arbitrary measurement.
Yeah, it obviously doesn't affect most of us but it seriously screws over those it does affect. That's really the only aspect of the FA I have issues with though.

The first computer I saw in a production work center was around '91. We were isolated from the rest of the Comm Sq, so we had a 2400 baud dial in line for email. Wordstar, dos 3.0, eventually dos 6. and Windows for Workgroups. Good times....
Yeahhhh, that sounds like the worst of times that one book was talking about. Lol.

25 years from now, when the world population is declining because of the prevalence of sexbots and holodecks, people will look back in horror at the thought of having to look at 60fps porn on the internet at pitiful speeds of 25M/s. It's all in the context of the time.
